moves.title: Integration by parts — worked example (∫ x e^{2x} dx)
moves.content: {"schemaVersion":"petros.render.v2","title":"Integration by parts — worked example (∫ x e^{2x} dx)","type":"worked_example","problemStatement":"Work through the integral ∫ x e^{2x} dx using integration by parts. Before we start, commit to which factor you would choose for u (the part to differentiate) and which for dv (the part to integrate).","steps":[{"id":"step-1-choose-u-dv","title":"Choose u and dv (make a quick commitment)","explanation":"Decide which part of the product x · e^{2x} you will set as u (to differentiate) and which as dv (to integrate). A common heuristic: choose u as the algebraic factor that simplifies when differentiated (here x).","predictionPrompt":"Which will you pick for u and dv? Type your choice, e.g., 'u = x, dv = e^{2x} dx'."},{"id":"step-2-differentiate-and-integrate","title":"Compute du and v","explanation":"Differentiate u to get du, and integrate dv to get v. If u = x, then du = dx. If dv = e^{2x} dx, then v = ∫ e^{2x} dx = (1/2) e^{2x}.","predictionPrompt":"Before proceeding, predict the expressions for du and v (one-line): du = ___, v = ___."},{"id":"step-3-substitute-into-formula","title":"Apply the integration-by-parts formula","explanation":"Use ∫ u dv = u v − ∫ v du. Substitute u, v, du: ∫ x e^{2x} dx = x · (1/2)e^{2x} − ∫ (1/2)e^{2x} · 1 dx = (1/2) x e^{2x} − (1/2) ∫ e^{2x} dx.","predictionPrompt":"Predict the intermediate result after substitution (before simplifying the remaining integral)."},{"id":"step-4-evaluate-and-simplify","title":"Evaluate the remaining integral and simplify","explanation":"Compute the remaining integral: ∫ e^{2x} dx = (1/2)e^{2x}. So ∫ x e^{2x} dx = (1/2) x e^{2x} − (1/2) · (1/2) e^{2x} + C = (1/2) x e^{2x} − (1/4) e^{2x} + C. Factor if desired: = e^{2x} ( (1/2) x − 1/4 ) + C.","predictionPrompt":"Predict the final simplified antiderivative (one-line): ____ + C."}],"finalCheck":"State which choice of u you used and why; then write the final antiderivative for ∫ x e^{2x} dx.","sourceGrounding":[{"label":"Standard calculus integration-by-parts formula","reference":"Any introductory calculus textbook; ∫ u dv = u v − ∫ v du"}]}

moves.title: Quick predict-and-reveal: choose u
moves.content: {"schemaVersion":"petros.render.v2","title":"Quick predict-and-reveal: choose u","type":"predict_then_reveal","prompt":"I'll show a short integral. Before I reveal the instructor's next step, type which part you'd choose as u (the other part will be dv). Integral: ∫ x^2 e^{x} dx. Which subexpression would you pick for u? (Answer briefly, e.g. 'u = x^2' or 'u = e^x')","reveal":"Instructor's next step: choose u = x^2 and dv = e^x dx. Then du = 2x dx and v = e^x. Substituting into integration by parts gives: ∫ x^2 e^x dx = x^2 e^x - ∫ 2x e^x dx. (You would apply integration by parts again on ∫2x e^x dx.)","explanation":"Why this reveal? Choose the polynomial factor (x^2) as u because polynomials simplify when differentiated, while e^x is easy to integrate — this follows the common heuristic (LIATE). If you answered 'u = e^x' instead, the resulting du stays e^x dx and you'd need to integrate x^2, which is less helpful for reducing the integral. Now compare: did your choice match the revealed u? If yes, briefly say why; if not, note whether the revealed next step changes how you'd proceed and then compute the remaining integral by applying integration by parts once more to ∫2x e^x dx."}
moves.studentSafeReason: A short prediction activity engages you to choose u vs dv on a new integral before revealing the correct next step, giving a diagnostic signal and keeping interaction brief.
decisionFactors: Topic profile recommends a predict-then-reveal item after a worked example for practice.
Only one move remaining; a single short prediction gives high diagnostic value for procedural skill.
Student persona 'fast_confident' responds well to quick commitments and immediate feedback.
Time remaining (~13 minutes) supports a quick prediction plus reveal and brief discussion.
moves.expectedEvidence: Student makes a quick choice for which part of the integrand to take as u (short answer), then upon reveal performs or explains the next integration-by-parts step (compute du and v) and whether the revealed choice matches their reasoning.
